text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- "The flags of national minorities in front of local municipality in Gostivar will not be taken over by force. We will wait for the (new flag) law to be passed by parliament," says Macedonian Justice Minister Georgi Spasov.

- Gostivar Mayor Rufi Osmani said the government's proposal does not fulfill the needs of Albanians. "We have yet to decide what our next actions will be. This draft law represents a degradation of our rights which were at a higher level even during communism," says Osmani.
- If the local municipal council does not respect the (flag) law, the government will dissolve it and initiate criminal proceedings against the mayor, says Spasov.
- The largest Macedonian opposition party VMRO-DPMNE welcomed the draft law (on flags on national minorities) and wonders why it was not adopted in 1991.
- Macedonian President Kiro Gligorov on third day of official visit to China, discusses possibilities for economic cooperation. Gligorov to visit Shanghai on Friday.
- Macedonian parliament on Wednesday adopts two laws necessary for receiving the first part of a $60 million Structural Adjustment Loan (SAL) arrangement.

- Ethnic Albanian PDPA and NDP parties unite under one name, the Democratic Party of Albanians. PDPA leader Arben Dzaferi says the move was necessary in order to reach national unity to achieve Albanians' national demands.

- Strike of employees in the judicial system continues. The government rejects strikers' demands, explaining that salaries from the state budget are low. -- Mircela Casule, Skopje newsroom +381 11 222 4305
